quote: I just got a few questions to get started. Is that okay?
stewart_read: Rep skips the interest_question (verified as skipped) and goes straight into a rapid-fire qualifier list, never establishing why the customer should care or what her interest in solar was.
coaching_implication: Ask 'what interested you in solar' before qualifiers — this is the emotional anchor the schema requires and it was skipped entirely.

stewart_read: The co-owner question got an unintelligible answer; rep never confirmed whether a spouse/co-owner exists, which risks a structurally excluded decision-maker at appointment time.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the mumbled answer as a 'no' and moved on strategically, but there's no evidence of that judgment — the transcript shows confusion, not resolution.
coaching_implication: Re-ask directly: 'Is anyone else on the title with you?' and get a clear yes/no before proceeding.

quote: Yeah. No. I'm at work right now. Yes, ma'am.
stewart_read: Customer clearly signals she's at work and possibly not able to focus; rep does not acknowledge this or offer to call back at a better time, just keeps running the script.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be strategically pushing through because the call is short and closing bill capture now avoids a second callback — but the resulting bill data is unreliable, undermining that strategy.
coaching_implication: When a customer discloses being at work/distracted, acknowledge it and offer a callback window — better data quality than pushing through confusion.

stewart_read: Rep never reflects the $300/month bill back to the customer as a pain point or hook — it's captured and immediately buried under a kWh usage question.
coaching_implication: Flip the $300 bill into a pain point ('so you're paying about $3,600 a year to the utility') before moving to kWh — creates the emotional anchor the schema calls for.

quote: Oh, are you able to ask? About Tesla, solar. Right?
stewart_read: Customer proactively asks about the Tesla partnership — a spontaneous curiosity signal — but rep gives a one-line confirmation and moves straight back to the bill-collection script.
coaching_implication: This was a live curiosity opening; rep could have briefly built on it ('yep, we're their certified installer partner') to build legitimacy/excitement instead of a flat 'Yeah... Yes.'

quote: I'll call you, and then we'll schedule you. Okay? Okay. Okay. Okay. Have a great day.
stewart_read: Call ends with no date, no time, no 'is that fair' handshake — just a promise to call back after she sends a bill photo.
coaching_implication: Even a soft callback needs a locked window: 'I'll call you tomorrow at 5pm once you're home, does that work?'
